items.prompt: Where does a B-tree grow taller?
hints: Think about what happens when a split reaches the top.
New levels are only ever added above the root.
When the root splits, its middle key becomes a new root, so the tree grows at the top.

options.text: At the root, when the root splits
options.feedback: Right. Growing at the top keeps every leaf on the same level.

options.text: At the leaves, like a binary search tree
options.feedback: That is how a BST grows. A B-tree never adds a level below its leaves.
An overflow splits a node and pushes a key up, but a new level appears only when the root splits.

items.prompt: Why are all the leaves of a B-tree always on the same level?
hints: Height changes only at the root: a root split adds a level, a root merge removes one.
Every leaf moves down or up together, so they always stay level.

options.text: The height only ever changes at the root, so every leaf moves together
options.feedback: Yes. That is balance without any extra work.

options.text: After every insert, rotations rebalance the tree
options.feedback: Rotations are how AVL and red-black trees stay balanced. B-trees split and merge instead.
Splitting a leaf creates a new leaf, on the same level as the old one.

items.prompt: What is the time complexity of searching a B-tree that holds n keys?
hints: How does the height grow as n grows?
Each node has at least ⌈m/2⌉ children, so the height is logarithmic in n.
A search visits one node per level, and there are O(log n) levels: O(log n).

options.feedback: Right. The height grows logarithmically, and a search visits one node per level.
That is scanning every key. A B-tree skips whole subtrees at each level.
The cost does grow with n, just very slowly.

items.prompt: You insert 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in that order into an empty order-3 B-tree. How tall is the tree?
hints: Insert one key at a time and split whenever a node reaches 3 keys.
A split pushes the middle key up. A root split makes a new root.

options.feedback: Yes. A BST built from the same sorted keys would be a 5-level chain.
That is the BST built from sorted keys. A B-tree splits instead of growing a chain.
The second split adds 4 to the root, which still has room, so no new level.
